updates.note: Announced the wastewater norovirus signal and rising stomach-illness visits (Mon., Sept. 20); said it is too early to say how any one person got sick; gave boil, hand-washing (sanitizer not enough) and stay-home guidance.
Beat: remote access to cargo systems under scrutiny; explained what tanker cargo-control systems do and that shore-based vendor support is common.

First on-record statement (Mon., Sept. 20) that investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems with federal cyber teams assisting; "will not characterize the cause" until the investigation supports a conclusion.
Rendal Terminals "cooperating fully with the Unified Command and with federal investigators"; no comment on substance.
National story on the remote-access line of inquiry; no attribution, notes officials did not say who, if anyone, accessed the systems.
Told the national wire "We are not going to get ahead of the investigation."
First public comment: CISA is supporting the Coast Guard, helping investigators and the companies involved understand "whether and how those systems were reached"; too early for findings.
Reminds readers A&R never reports aircraft numbers or schedules; pointed families to family readiness contacts.

Beat: drone statement (Mon., Sept. 20): "aware of the reports of drones... working with the appropriate authorities... no impact to operations"; welcomed aircraft back and thanked Fort Worth hosts; declined to discuss security measures.
Beat: residents' drone-light videos; Harborline 6 reviewed several of Ortega's clips (small steady and blinking lights).
Monday drone statement re-quoted for Harborline 6; Navy not discussing security measures.

Beat: TV interview (Tue., Sept. 21). Filmed lights over NAS on several nights since the storm, first video posted the week before; "I'm not saying what they are"; keeps camera time stamps on; shoots from a backyard tripod.
"We know how hard this is, and we're sorry"; crews working around the clock; will give a timeline "when we have one we can stand behind."

Runs her Calallen street's water runs with a clipboard (house numbers, household size, who has a car, who can't lift) and a garden wagon; neighbors include an older couple two doors down and a family on the corner with a newborn; frustrated by "soon" with no timeline; puts boiled water and soap by doors.
Advised shoreline residents with cough, sore throat, headaches or rash to get checked; wash oil off with soap and water, not solvents; don't clean up oiled areas yourself.
Says the oil smell is fainter but still there; "my throat's been raw for days"; staying inside with windows shut; asks who pays neighbors' doctor bills; welded his whole working life around fuel.
Market can price a hurricane but not the open question about how two tankers' cargo systems behaved; "Corpus Christi isn't a side door for U.S. crude. It's the front door."
Beat: stomach illness surge.
Beat: GI illness advisory (Wed., Sept. 22): most recover at home in a day or two; ER is for dehydration or severe illness; listed warning signs.

Beat: hallway beds for GI patients (Wed., Sept. 22). "Every stretcher in the hallway is somebody who can't keep water down"; twelve-hour shifts since the storm; asks people to bring a water bottle and charger and be patient with the front desk.
Explained remote maintenance and credentials "like keys"; noted the statement named no vessel.
"We are aware of the company's statement"; will not characterize any party's role.

First public statement (Wed., Sept. 22): "Our remote-maintenance credentials were misused. That should not have been possible, and we own that"; revoked all remote access for every customer; cooperating; no connection restored until safe; "We're a small company."
Service quotes: stomach bug passes in a day or two for most healthy adults; knock on older neighbors' doors.
"Getting aircraft home is the first step"; no schedules or numbers.

"Our people are the mission here"; workforce to return as buildings are cleared and safe, employees hear it from supervisors first; no return date; did not describe which aircraft or components were in damaged hangars.

First statement (Thu., Sept. 23): "We can confirm we are investigating reports of drones near Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. We have no further comment at this time." Would not say when the probe began or what was found.
Reaction to FBI probe: "That's all I wanted, for someone to take it seriously"; has kept his original files with time stamps; "I'm a guy with a telescope."
Noted the Coast Guard has not publicly linked any company to the investigation.
Investigation continues; will not characterize any party's role.

Beat: company statement/interview (Thu., Sept. 23). "I don't know who did this, and I'm not going to guess"; described planned changes before restoring any connection (scheduled sessions, crew approval on board, watched in real time, closed when done; "No standing access"); won't discuss specific vessels while the investigation is open.
Explainer on roles (Navy inside the fence, FBI, FAA airspace rules, police take reports) and why officials say little.
"We don't discuss security measures... we're aware and we're working with the appropriate authorities."
Repeated confirmation of the investigation; no further comment.
"Marsh cleanup is slow on purpose"; boom to keep oil out of sensitive areas; don't pick up oiled birds, call the hotline.
"A beach is a parking lot. A marsh is a sponge"; heavy equipment can do more harm than the oil; how long oil lingers depends on plants, mud and tidal flushing; "we'll be learning as we go."
Ledger filed a Texas Public Information Act request for the Vantorra contract and related records; promised a Sunday explainer.

Defended moving fast: "You can't run a months-long bid process while that sits at the curb"; curbside debris guidance (curb not street, away from drains, hydrants, mailboxes, power lines; separate piles); routes to be posted on official county channels.

First public appearance (Fri., Sept. 24): Vantorra won the county's $14.2M sole-source debris contract; "We're going to be working around the clock... get this mess off their curbs"; gave no details on crews or equipment.
Announced (Fri., Sept. 24) damaged pumps need replacement parts and temporary pumps can't match plant pumps; "We're sorry"; date only when "we can stand behind" it; asks patience for crews.
Weekly roundup; thanked spouses running carpools and water runs.
"Every day we get a little closer to normal"; asked families to report anything unusual and not speculate online.
"Take care of your homes and your families... you'll hear it from your supervisor first."
Quoted confirming the investigation; no further comment.
Explained wastewater surveillance: people shed norovirus before or without symptoms; "a trend line, not a diagnosis"; "Everybody uses the sewer. That makes it one of the fairest measures we have."
"We remain aware of the reports and continue to work with the appropriate authorities... no impact to operations."
"Nothing the last few nights. Just stars and the usual planes"; still looking; will hand over his files if investigators want them.
Explained why sorting speeds pickup; routes to be posted on official county channels.

Beat: ribbon-cutting style quote (Sat., Sept. 25): "This is what we do... folks are going to see trucks on their streets... We're going to get it gone"; no start date, truck count or crew breakdown; will follow the county's schedule.

Beat: sole-source emergency contracts explainer (Sun., Sept. 26). Notes a sole-source award is not by itself a red flag; lists records to watch (contract, load tickets, monitoring logs, invoices, amendments); Ledger files requests on every major emergency contract.
"Emergency doesn't mean no rules. It means you can move faster on the front end. You still document everything on the back end."
Came to the hub for water and stayed to sort donations; "Here nobody asks you for paperwork... Tres. Okay, here."; lives a few blocks from the church.

Fellowship hall hub: bilingual sign "Take what you need. Bring what you can."; greets people by name with her penciled binder; "This is the front door of this neighborhood right now"; preached from a podium between water pallets; "Faith is a verb this month"; invites officials to "come sit at my table."
"The channel will reopen when it is safe for vessel traffic"; depends on waterway conditions including the spill response; nothing new on the remote-access investigation.

Boat came through the storm with little more than scraped paint; tied up at the dock in Aransas Pass; walks its deck every morning like his father did; found oil on his nets the week of the storm; owes on the boat and the fuel dock; has a deckhand with two kids; "Shrimp in the water don't pay the bank"; won't sell the boat yet.
Announced stomach-illness visits easing (Tue., Sept. 28): "We're seeing the curve bend down... It is not the all-clear"; no new counts.
"Monday night, for a few hours, the hallway was empty... I actually ate lunch sitting down."
Beat: who gets help first; ties pre-storm transit gaps, evacuation bus waits and 911 call concentration to residents' reports of waiting.

Beat (waits days for help, reported Tue., Sept. 28): "Nadie vino. Nobody came, not for days... I'm not saying nobody cared. I'm saying nobody came"; ran out of ice, water, phone battery; got water from Whitfield's hall; "who's checking on us?"

"We had water and food on the table before anybody official was on this block. That's not a brag. That's a problem"; no car, no phone battery, language barriers mean people wait; keeping her own list of needs.
Column (Tue., Sept. 28): Rafael is her third hurricane covering the city; calls on county and city to measure and publish wait times by neighborhood; "Measuring is not blaming."
Mentioned in Treviño's column for keeping a handwritten list of neighbors' needs.

Shop gutted by surge; hand-painted plywood sign "OPEN-ISH"; selling ice, hooks and tackle from a folding table; tearing out drywall with a crowbar; "I rode out two storms in this shop. This one I left for, and it still rode me"; fields calls asking what's open and tells them what the state says; adjusters scheduling and contractors booked; has fished the jetties since boyhood (sheepshead in winter, tarpon in August); undecided on how much to rebuild.
Fact-check separates the false "aid only for the wealthy" claim from documented delays in bay neighborhoods.
Rumor control: "Help goes to people who need it, period. If you've been waiting, we want to know where you are"; "If someone believes aid isn't for them, they won't ask."
Named as one account spreading the false claim that aid will go only to wealthy neighborhoods; debunked.
Reported the researcher's findings with what-to-do guidance; earlier rumors listed with corrections.

Beat: coordinated rumor network analysis (Thu., Sept. 30): about 40 accounts, posts pointed to the same lookalike aid site used in phishing emails; "Same site, same lure"; won't guess who is behind it: "Attribution is for governments."
National framing of the rumor-network finding; no attribution.
To national wire: "The pattern is the point... all roads lead to the same fake site"; "Governments attribute. Researchers describe."
Families roundup; urged service members to report suspicious emails through command procedures; shared a reader's photo of youth football practice with a sideline water cooler and hand-washing jug.
"We continue to work with the appropriate authorities, and there's no impact to operations."

Tapes faucets with blue painter's tape beside a jug of boiled water; describes what a classroom needs under a boil-water notice (a person, a jug with a spigot, soap, paper towels); "When it gets better, that's when people stop doing the thing that made it better"; fridge sign "Tap = NO. Jug = YES. Soap = ALWAYS"; "We'll take normal-ish."
Debris how-to: "Every pile that's sorted and in the right place is a pile a truck can grab and go"; don't call 911 about pickup; "County crews don't ask you for money."
Profiling the Elizondo family over the season.

Profile (Sun., Oct. 3): boils water in one big pot every morning since Sept. 18 ("Three kids, one pot"); helps older and disabled clients bathe, eat, take medicine; gets to clients by bus when it runs and neighbors' rides when it doesn't; a youth-group boy from Whitfield's church brought a case of water by bicycle after the storm; strict about soap and boiled water with clients; "Send the bus early. Knock on the door."
Laughed about the youth-group boy on the bicycle delivering water: "He's earned a medal."

Cutting out wet drywall at about two feet himself; carpet, a recliner, two doors and a mattress at the curb; keeps windows shut and a mask on while working; lends tools to neighbors and keeps a notebook of who has what; to-do list on the fridge; "Tired is better than scared."
Reported the fuel contract from federal records; noted emergency awards are common and not by themselves a sign of a problem; Ledger tracking all emergency contracts since the storm.

First public appearance (Mon., Oct. 4): "Quellmar is proud to support the air station... Our product meets specifications"; did not say when deliveries began, how much fuel the contract covers or how long it runs.
Named the supplier as Delta Pumps & Controls; service guidance.

Beat: pump parts delayed (Mon., Oct. 4): supplier's local warehouse "took on water in the same storm we did"; parts coming from out of state; no arrival date; notice lifted only after installation and testing say it's safe.
Beat: fishery closure impacts.
Respiratory complaints near shorelines easing; keep avoiding contact with oil.
Closure extended (Tue., Oct. 5) "about protecting the public"; won't reopen until testing shows seafood safe; no new reopening date.
"Every week is a payment I don't make. Every week my deckhand looks for other work. Tell me a number. I can plan around a number."; "I can see it. I just can't touch it."
City in contact with the supplier; parts must be installed and the system tested before the notice is lifted.

Beat: explains the delay (Tue., Oct. 5): "Our local warehouse flooded in the same storm"; parts coming from out of state; "I live here. I'm boiling my water too"; won't promise a day until she sees a tracking number; "I'd rather tell the city the truth late than a lie early."
Respiratory complaints near shorelines easing (Tue., Oct. 5); people with asthma or COPD or lingering symptoms should see a doctor; don't eat fish or shellfish from the closed bays.
Opened his windows for the first time in a while; "Smell's mostly gone on my street... My throat's better"; will walk the beach when officials say it's clean.
"The rumor makes you mad, then the link offers you a fix... If a post makes your blood boil, that's the moment to stop and check."
"We remain aware of the reports and we continue to work with the appropriate authorities... no impact to operations."
"Most nights now, it's just the sky"; wants officials eventually to say "here's what it was, here's what you can stop worrying about"; still sets up his tripod; kept original files.
"The investigation is active and thorough, and we will not release partial information."
CISA continues to support the Coast Guard; declined to discuss the case; general advice: know what's connected, keep it patched, know who can get in from outside, turn off what you don't need.

Profile (Thu., Oct. 7): keeps a granola bar in each scrub pocket (one for a teammate); twelve-hour shifts since Sept. 14; runs the floor as charge nurse; "You learn to triage the hallway"; hallway mostly empty since late September; a church sent food trays; "wash your hands... until I'm fifty"; never discusses individual patients.
Weekly roundup; pointed families to Military OneSource and installation family support counseling.
To A&R: "We're glad to help keep the station supplied while its regular supplier recovers."
"We hear Calallen, and we hear everyone"; won't lift the notice until water is tested and safe.

Added a "Heard anything?" column to her clipboard; liked that the city gave a reason for the delay ("A warehouse flooded. Okay. That's a reason"); wants the city to write down what broke and fix it "so the next teacher doesn't have to do this with a clipboard."
Many neighbors fish from piers and seawalls to stretch grocery budgets; hall added canned fish and beans; "If the bay can't feed us for a while, we'll feed each other."
"The marsh keeps a diary"; seafood testing is "the bridge between the science and the dinner table"; won't guess timelines; wants monitoring to include seawall and pier fishing spots.

Column (Sun., Oct. 10): paddles the bays when not writing about them; supports the extended closure but calls for published testing plans, partial-reopening criteria and regular updates in English, Spanish and Vietnamese at the docks.
Cited in Navarro's column: "tell me a number, and I can plan around a number."
Now volunteers two hours sorting donations on her days off: "Pastora gave me water when I needed it. Now I give two hours. That's the deal."

Hub now on a laminated schedule (water Mon/Wed/Fri, food boxes Tue/Sat, rides: ask Pastor); needs shifted to mold supplies, fans, insurance letters, rides; her list is longer, not shorter; wants to hand it to someone official: "I'll even make you a plate."
Analysis built only from public figures; lists what is still unknown (insured and uninsured losses, business closures, timelines for channel and bays).
"Every week the channel is closed is a week of revenue that doesn't come back... the lost weeks are lost."

Warns of boil-water fatigue: "This is the dangerous part of a long boil-water notice"; reminders on coffee makers, ice makers, produce, dishwashing, bathing babies, pets; "Nobody gets a medal for the last week of a boil-water notice."
Shop walls stripped to the studs with his pencil notes on the bare wood; 'OPEN-ISH' sign; selling ice and tackle.
Month-after checklist of open and closed items.
"We are ready when the Coast Guard is"; lining up berths, pilots and terminals; declined to give a reopening date.
"The first day isn't the story. The story is how fast the backlog clears"; remote-access probe on traders' minds: "everyone's asking their own terminals what's connected to what."
